extracted.intended_audience: web managers, content strategists, and digital teams producing public-facing government content
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating clear, audience-focused plain language content for government websites, including writing, content design, and testing to ensure public understanding and legal compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plain language – content that is clear and easy to understand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plain language is critical to helping the public make sense of their obligations and benefits. It makes content more efficient and effective. Aim for clarity and ease of understanding in all public-facing content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain Writing Act compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plain Writing Act of 2010 established the requirement that content for the public is written for its specific audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content published for the public must be written for its specific audience to meet the legal requirement. Use these guides to align content creation, design, and testing with the Act's intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of plain language
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of plain language principles, writing for your audience, and the Plain Writing Act of 2010.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers core principles for plain language and audience-focused writing. Use this overview to ground decisions about tone, structure, word choice, and purpose before drafting content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing for understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of how to write clear content that follows plain language guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on actionable writing techniques to make content clear and understandable (e.g., plain word choice, logical structure, clear sentences). Apply these techniques when drafting and editing copy intended for public audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design for understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: How content design can support plain language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how layout, headings, visual hierarchy, and other content-design decisions support readability and comprehension. Use design to make content scannable and to highlight key actions and information for users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test for understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn how to test that your content is easily understandable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes methods for evaluating whether content is understood by the target audience (e.g., user testing, comprehension checks). Incorporate testing into content workflows to validate clarity and make iterative improvements.
